summary.title: Build your own Search Engine from Scratch in Java
summary.one_liner: You learn how a basic search engine works (crawl, tokenize, lemmatize, build an in-memory inverted index, query it) by building a small Java/Dropwizard app called Orbit.
takeaways: An inverted index maps each term to the documents it appears in, which enables fast keyword lookup.
Indexing pipeline: fetch page, lowercase, tokenize, lemmatize, remove stop words and punctuation, then build the index.
A crawler needs a depth limit and a visited set to avoid endless or cyclic crawling and running out of memory.
The Orbit app exposes a crawl endpoint to submit URLs and a search endpoint that looks up query terms in the index.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a minimal search engine called Orbit in Java. It explains indexing with a phone-book analogy, then shows a step-by-step text pipeline (lowercasing, tokenizing, lemmatizing, removing stop words) using an example paragraph. The implementation uses Dropwizard for REST APIs, HtmlUnit for fetching pages, and the Stanford NLP library for tokenization, with an in-memory HashMap as the inverted index. It covers a crawl API with depth and crawlChildren options, and a search API that splits the query and returns matching documents. It ends with steps to run the project from GitHub in IntelliJ.
